value.name: Asha asks about missed deposit consequences
value.description: Asha calls Claire and asks exactly what will happen if the deposit is not paid by Monday.
evidence: "Claire," she said, keeping her voice in the register she used when she wanted a witness to hear only the question, "tell me exactly what happens if the deposit isn't paid by Monday."

value.name: Claire reveals fallback placement deadline
value.description: Claire quietly explains that the room will be released at 12:01, the waitlist will resume, and state-default placement is the fallback referral.
evidence: the room would be released at twelve-oh-one, the waitlist resumed, and the intake coordinator had already flagged the state-default placement as the fallback referral

value.name: Asha learns Marcus withheld paperwork
value.description: Asha realizes the paperwork had been sitting on Marcus's side of the desk for nine days, showing he had withheld important information.
evidence: the paperwork sitting in a folder she had seen on Marcus's side of the desk for nine days
Asha registered the nine days the way she registered the four-month-old: another number Marcus had been sitting on while looking her in the face.

value.name: Asha recognizes Marcus's deception
value.description: Asha understands that Marcus has been withholding key facts from her and that she now has more of the picture than he intended.
evidence: she only let the refrigerator cycle under the silence and understood that whatever she decided in the next thirty-six hours, she was deciding it with more of the picture than Marcus had ever intended her to have.

value.name: Asha demands to speak with Marcus
value.description: After absorbing the consequences, Asha asks Claire to put Marcus on the phone.
evidence: "Claire," she said, "can you put Marcus on the phone?"

value.name: Claire hesitates before returning to Marcus
value.description: Claire falls silent as she weighs the consequences of walking back to Marcus and what he will read on her face.
evidence: On the other end the hall went very still, the kind of stillness a person makes when she is calculating which door she will have to walk back through and what the man behind it will read in her face.
